newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 25.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Friday:
* Columbia/HCA Chief Executive Richard Scott may step down amid an investigation into the company's billing practices.
* Microsoft is preparing to enter markets that have traditionally been the province of large computer systems vendors.
* America Online backed off its plan to begin providing lists of its customers' telephone numbers to telemarketers.
* Delta Air Lines trumpeted record profits of $886 million for the last fiscal year and named two interim replacements for ousted chief executive Ronald Allen.
* Digital Equipment reported quarterly operating earnings that more than doubled from a year earlier.
* The Dow industrials, down nearly 100 points at one point, ended 28.57 points higher at another record 8,116.93.
* Silicon Graphics reported earnings that exceeded Wall Street expectations by a large margin.
* Xerox earnings rose 15 percent in the second quarter.
* At Home Network is expected to announce a service that will enable Internet users to download high-quality audio recordings within minutes over its high-speed cable connections.
* An appeals court ruled that Microsoft could not exclude some freelance workers from a stock-purchase plan, in a case closely watched by other high technology companies.
* The dollar rose against the mark for the fourth straight day.
* The American Cancer Society said it would not back the proposed tobacco settlement unless it is toughened.
